guidance: Manual or model-driven teaching evaluation. Record direct evidence before changing not_run; package tests and an edited existing course do not establish fresh teaching behavior.

cases.startingPrompt: Teach me how awaiting a coroutine differs from scheduling a task. Keep the scope focused.
learnerActions: Read the lesson and overview
Find the concept again using the keyword index
Trace both demonstrated behaviors
forbiddenShortcuts: Mandatory visible Outcome section
Skip async fundamentals because Python experience is intermediate
Show only awaiting while assessing scheduling
Pad reading or duplicate nearby prose in the recap
requiredObservedEvidence: Concrete Keywords section and matching indexed lesson link
Problem introduced before unfamiliar terms
Clear explanations and examples of both behaviors
Proportionate recap and separate practice estimate

cases.startingPrompt: Give me an assignment implementing a small concurrent client simulation.
learnerActions: Identify the question, constraints and files to submit
Distinguish required behavior from design choices
Inspect written questions and scoring placement
forbiddenShortcuts: General theory essay duplicating the quiz
Require notes when the artifact already supplies the evidence
Rubric table before task/submission/next-step instructions
Hide expected behavior in private scoring criteria
requiredObservedEvidence: Question-shaped task with input/output and failure expectations
Clear deliverables, constraints, choices and observable checks
Written explanations only about this implementation when needed
Detailed scoring private or in the final section; answer key private

initialLearnerContext.experience: can await and schedule simple coroutines; has not built a service

cases.startingPrompt: Help me learn enough asyncio to build a local service with clients and background jobs.
learnerActions: Review the lesson and practice sequence
Complete a small handler task
Extend it with a client
Continue remaining practice after the final lesson
Integrate the final service
forbiddenShortcuts: Jump directly from sleep simulation to a whole service
Add empty lessons just to link assignments
Require rebuilding all prior work from scratch
Use conflicting protocols or circular prerequisites
Provide the complete capstone solution
requiredObservedEvidence: Manageable intermediate tasks add meaningful capabilities and reuse artifacts
Practical signatures, data shapes, relevant APIs and a starting order
Consistent behavior and protocol across lesson and briefs
Ordered next-assignment links through the capstone and finish checkpoint
Optional/required declarations agree with saved work indexes

initialLearnerContext.courseState: registered assignments with explicit optional and required flags

cases.startingPrompt: I finished this lesson. Continue with my next action.
learnerActions: Finish the required quiz
Observe the ready assignment offer
Defer optional practice
Resume with a pending question or ungraded submission
Finish the last lesson and continue the assignment chain
forbiddenShortcuts: Silently bypass assignments because quizzes passed
Make optional practice an unavoidable dependency
Overwrite a pending question
Treat ungraded submission as passed
Declare completion while required practice remains
requiredObservedEvidence: Explicit practice purpose, link and optional/required status at checkpoint
Deferral honored and alternative starting point for optional dependencies
Pending question and submitted evidence preserved
Next assignment offered after review even without a following lesson
Saved completion requirements and learner-facing status agree

initialLearnerContext.experience: basic Linux; new to container build practice

cases.startingPrompt: Give me hands-on practice changing a Dockerfile to preserve dependency cache reuse.
learnerActions: Locate the starting files and working directory
Identify relevant commands and first edit
Predict then optionally inspect the result
forbiddenShortcuts: Only repeat caching theory
Supply a complete Dockerfile solution
Assume Docker or network availability
Claim an unrun build succeeded
requiredObservedEvidence: Concrete entry points, relevant commands and expected observations
Provided resources and environment assumptions explicit
Direction leaves ordering and implementation work to the learner
Required static deliverables distinguished from optional runtime evidence

initialLearnerContext.courseState: partially completed course; old attempts and learner files exist; assignments index empty

cases.startingPrompt: Improve this course and add intermediate practice before its capstone. Preserve my work.
learnerActions: Record hashes of learner answers and existing keys
Inspect the revised practice sequence
Resume through the supported helper
Compare old progress and attempts
forbiddenShortcuts: Hand-edit state or historical records to register assignments
Reset old progress
Overwrite learner work
Claim practice is tracked when no assignment index exists
Retroactively add required completion work without agreement
requiredObservedEvidence: Explicit material revision and valid material hashes
Old learner files, keys and evidence preserved
Added practice links and tracking limits clearly described
Optional practice and saved course completion kept distinct
